title: Motorola's iPhone Duo rival is taking shape, and it could pack a surprise chipset
excerpt: A new Qualcomm chip could power the Razr
content_html:
Published Nov 19, 2026, 6:34 AM EST

Sanuj is a freelance tech journalist with over six years of experience covering smartphones, wearables, and consumer technology. He currently writes for Android Police, Tom's Guide, Android Central, Android Authority, and Pocket-lint. He has previously contributed to publications like Pocketnow and MakeUseOf. 

Since the start of 2025 alone, he has tested over 30 smartphones. He has also attended major global trade shows including MWC (2024, 2025, 2026) and IFA (2024, 2025), along with launch events hosted by Google, Samsung, and other leading Android brands.

When he's not writing about tech, you'll find him sipping a cup of chai, scrolling Twitter, and reading updates about his favorite football club, Chelsea FC.

Feel free to reach out to him via email at sanujb6 [at] gmail [dot] com.

Motorola is all set to reveal its iPhone Duo competitor soon, and a new leak has given us more details about the upcoming foldable smartphone.

2026 has largely been about the shift toward wider foldable smartphones. Until now, most foldable phones launched with a relatively tall form factor, but with the introduction of the iPhone Duo, and even before it, manufacturers have started moving toward wider designs that offer a more tablet-like experience when unfolded.

Samsung already jumped on the bandwagon with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 earlier this year, while Xiaomi also has its own Xiaomi 18 Fold. Previous leaks have revealed that Motorola is preparing to join the trend with the Razr Flex, and now more details about the device have surfaced.

Motorola's Razr Flex is shaping up to be a serious iPhone Duo rival

As spotted by Android Authority, a new security certification document has revealed that the Motorola Razr Flex will run Android 17 out of the box. The smartphone reportedly carries the codename Parker and model number XT2761. The document also reveals that the device will be powered by a Snapdragon chipset identified as SM8845 Pro.

Previous rumors suggested that the Razr Flex would run on the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 (SM8845), Qualcomm's previous-generation flagship chipset. However, the new certification document points toward the SM8845 Pro, which could be a more powerful version of the Snapdragon 8 Gen 5.

This chipset hasn't officially debuted yet, but it could launch alongside the Razr Flex. It's also worth noting that the security document mentions support for Bluetooth 6.0 out of the box and face unlock.

Alongside this leak, there's also a new leaked image circulating on Reddit that allegedly shows the Razr Flex 2027 from the back. Of course, the image hasn't been verified yet, but it suggests the phone could feature a horizontal camera housing with two cameras and a flash, alongside Motorola's familiar design elements.

The Motorola Razr Flex has already appeared on the company's own support website, so it's increasingly looking like a question of when Motorola will officially announce the device rather than if. Considering the previous listing included 2027 in the name, there's a good chance the company is preparing to unveil the foldable next year.

Of course, nothing has been officially confirmed just yet, but Motorola could be saving the Razr Flex for CES 2027, similar to how the company first showcased the Razr Fold at the tech event last year.
